topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students to the final course lecture and introduces the key aims and topics to be covered regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss conventional cancer treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively target malignant cells by exploiting their intrinsic defects in signaling dependencies, cell cycle checkpoints, and DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapies and kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concept of oncogene addiction, the development of small-molecule kinase inhibitors against driving mutations, and the clinical challenges of drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically bind cancer cell-surface targets and induce tumor cell destruction.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore tumor interactions with the immune system and detail methods of activating host T cells against cancer using checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of oncology by examining persistent therapeutic challenges, historical gains in survival, future clinical strategies, and the ethical dilemmas of trialing new treatments.
